summary: Extends the IMAP command for listing mailboxes so that one extensible LIST command can carry options and return extra information. Previously each extension needed its own special list command, and combining extensions was awkward. This standards-track document gives clients a single, consistent way to ask for lists of mailboxes with added details.

plainLanguage.summary: The IMAP LIST command asks a mail server which folders it has. This RFC gives that command options, so a client can ask in one go for subscribed folders, folders on other servers, several name patterns at once, and which folders have subfolders.

questions: how to list mailboxes with options in imap
subtitle: Extending the IMAP LIST command so a client can ask for subscribed, remote and hierarchical mailboxes in one query.

tldr.problem: IMAP clients had several separate commands for listing mailboxes, and no way to ask for several things at once or to say which mailbox names to look for.
tldr.mechanism: The LIST command gains selection options, return options, a list of mailbox patterns in parentheses, and extra fields at the end of each response. The extension is announced by the LIST-EXTENDED capability.
tldr.outcome: One command can now list subscribed mailboxes, include remote ones, match several patterns and report which parents have children. The older RLIST and RLSUB commands are signposted for retirement.

today: RFC 5258 is a Proposed Standard from June 2008, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It defines the LIST-EXTENDED capability, three selection options, two return options, five mailbox attributes and the CHILDINFO extended data item, and it announces the intent to retire the RLIST and RLSUB commands.

sections.title: What the Extension Changes
sections.content:
The LIST command is extended by amending the syntax to allow options and multiple patterns to be specified. The list of options replaces the several commands that are currently used to mix and match the information requested. The new syntax is backward compatible, with no ambiguity: the new syntax is being used if the first word after the command name begins with a parenthesis, if the second word after the command name begins with a parenthesis, or if the LIST command has more than 2 parameters. Otherwise the original syntax is used.

By adding options to the LIST command, the intent is announced to phase out and eventually deprecate the RLIST and RLSUB commands. The extension also defines the mechanism to request extended mailbox information, such as is described in the Child Mailbox Extension. The base LSUB command is not deprecated by this extension; rather, this extension adds a way to obtain subscription information with more options, in those server implementations that support it. Clients that simply need a list of subscribed mailboxes, as provided by the LSUB command, should continue to use that command.

This document defines an IMAP4 extension identified by the capability string LIST-EXTENDED. It makes the following changes to the IMAP4 protocol: it defines new syntax for LIST command options, extends LIST to allow for multiple mailbox patterns, adds the LIST command selection options SUBSCRIBED, REMOTE and RECURSIVEMATCH, adds the LIST command return options SUBSCRIBED and CHILDREN, adds the new mailbox attributes NonExistent, Subscribed, Remote, HasChildren and HasNoChildren, and adds the CHILDINFO extended data item.
sections.plainLanguage: The old LIST command had a fixed shape and separate commands for some jobs. The new one keeps the old shape working and adds options around it. A server that supports the extension says so in its capability list, and a client must not use an option the server has not advertised.

sections.title: The Extended LIST Command
sections.content:
The extension updates the syntax of the LIST command to allow for multiple mailbox patterns to be specified if they are enclosed in parentheses. A mailbox name matches a list of mailbox patterns if it matches at least one mailbox pattern. If a mailbox name matches multiple patterns, the server should return only a single LIST response. Some servers might restrict which patterns are allowed; if a server does not accept a particular pattern, it must silently ignore it.

The LIST command syntax is also extended in two additional ways: by adding a parenthesized list of command options between the command name and the reference name, which are the selection options, and an optional list of options at the end that control what kind of information should be returned, which are the return options.

A selection option tells the server which mailbox names should be selected by the LIST operation. The server should return information about all mailbox names that match the canonical LIST pattern and satisfy any additional selection criteria specified by the selection options. When multiple selection options are specified, the server must return information about mailbox names that satisfy every selection option, unless a description of a particular option prescribes special rules.

A return option controls which information is returned for each matched mailbox name. Return options must not cause the server to report information about additional mailbox names. If the client has not specified any return option, only information about attributes should be returned.

Each selection and return option is enabled by a capability string, and a client must not send an option for which the server has not advertised support. A server must respond to options it does not recognize with a BAD response. The client should not specify any option more than once, and if it does, the server must act as if it received the option only once.
sections.plainLanguage: The command gains three parts: a bracketed list of options before the mailbox name, the mailbox name itself, and an optional RETURN list at the end. The options before the name narrow what is looked for; the options at the end say what extra information to report about each one found.

sections.title: Selection Options
sections.content:
SUBSCRIBED causes the LIST command to list subscribed names rather than the existing mailboxes. This will often be a subset of the actual mailboxes, and the list may contain names of mailboxes that do not exist. The list must include exactly those mailbox names that match the canonical list pattern and are subscribed to. The option is intended to supplement the LSUB command, and of particular note are the mailbox attributes as returned by this option compared with what LSUB returns. With LSUB the attributes returned may not reflect the actual status of the mailbox name, and the NoSelect attribute has a second special meaning, indicating that the mailbox is not itself subscribed but has descendant mailboxes that are. With the SUBSCRIBED selection option the attributes are accurate and complete and have no special meanings. Clients should therefore continue to use LSUB unless they specifically want the additional information offered by LIST (SUBSCRIBED). The option also implies the SUBSCRIBED return option.

REMOTE causes the LIST command to show remote mailboxes as well as local ones. It is intended to replace the RLIST command and, with the SUBSCRIBED selection option, the RLSUB command. It has no interaction with other options: its effect is to tell the server to apply the other options, if any, to remote mailboxes in addition to local ones. A request for REMOTE RECURSIVEMATCH is invalid, because a request for RECURSIVEMATCH alone is.

RECURSIVEMATCH forces the server to return information about parent mailboxes that do not match the other selection options but have some submailboxes that do. Information about children is returned in the CHILDINFO extended data item. For a parent mailbox to be returned it still has to match the canonical LIST pattern. The option must not occur as the only selection option, or only with REMOTE, as it only makes sense when other selection options are also used; the server must return a BAD tagged response in that case.
sections.plainLanguage: SUBSCRIBED asks for the folders the user has ticked, even if the folder has since been deleted. REMOTE adds folders that live on another server. RECURSIVEMATCH adds the parent folders that hold matching children, so the client can show a tree.

sections.title: Return Options and New Attributes
sections.content:
The SUBSCRIBED return option causes the LIST command to return subscription state for all matching mailbox names. The Subscribed attribute must be supported and accurately computed when it is specified, and all mailbox flags must be accurately computed, which differs from the behaviour of the LSUB command.

The CHILDREN return option requests mailbox child information as originally proposed in the Child Mailbox Extension. It is simply an indication that the client wants this information, and a server may provide it even if the option is not specified. It gives a client an efficient way to determine whether a particular mailbox has children, without issuing a separate list for each mailbox name. It defines two new attributes that must be returned within a LIST response: HasChildren, whose presence indicates that the mailbox has child mailboxes, and HasNoChildren, whose presence indicates that the mailbox has no child mailboxes accessible to the currently authenticated user. It is an error for the server to return both attributes in the same response. The HasNoChildren attribute should not be confused with the IMAP4 attribute NoInferiors, which indicates that no child mailboxes exist now and none can be created in the future.

The extension also defines new mailbox attributes. The NonExistent attribute indicates that a mailbox name does not refer to an existing mailbox. It is not meaningful by itself: names that match the pattern but do not exist must not be returned unless the name also satisfies the selection criteria, or RECURSIVEMATCH was specified and the name has at least one descendant that does match the pattern and does satisfy the criteria. In practice NonExistent is usually returned with one or more of Subscribed, Remote, HasChildren, or the CHILDINFO extended data item. It implies NoSelect, and it must be supported and accurately computed. The Subscribed attribute indicates that a mailbox name is subscribed to, the Remote attribute indicates that a mailbox is a remote mailbox, and both must be accurately computed when their options are specified.
sections.plainLanguage: The response can now say more than before. A name can be marked as subscribed, as living on another server, as not existing, and as having or not having subfolders. The last two are what lets a client draw a folder tree without listing everything twice.

sections.title: When the Server Returns a Response
sections.content:
Several principles guide server implementations in deciding whether a LIST response should be returned, how many responses, and what information they may contain. At most one LIST response should be returned for each mailbox name that matches the canonical LIST pattern. Server implementors must not assume that clients will be able to assemble mailbox attributes and other information returned in multiple LIST responses.

There are only two reasons for including a matching mailbox name in the responses: the mailbox name also satisfies the selection criteria, or the mailbox name does not satisfy the selection criteria but has at least one descendant mailbox name that does satisfy them and that does not match the canonical LIST pattern. The CHILDINFO extended data item can only be returned when the RECURSIVEMATCH selection option is specified. Attributes returned in the same LIST response must be treated additively, so a response carrying \Subscribed and \NonExistent for the mailbox Fruit/Peach means that the mailbox does not exist but is subscribed.

All clients that support this extension must treat an attribute with a stronger meaning as implying any attribute that can be inferred from it. The NoInferiors attribute implies the HasNoChildren attribute, and the NonExistent attribute implies the NoSelect attribute.

The CHILDINFO extended data item describes the selection criteria that caused it to be returned and indicates that the mailbox has at least one descendant mailbox that matches the selection criteria. The LSUB command indicates this condition with the NoSelect attribute, but LIST (SUBSCRIBED) must not do that, since NoSelect keeps its original meaning here. Servers should only return a non-matching mailbox name along with CHILDINFO if at least one matching child is not also being returned, so redundant CHILDINFO responses should be suppressed.
sections.plainLanguage: The server sends one response per matching name, never several that the client would have to merge. A name appears either because it matches the criteria itself or because one of its children does, and the latter case is flagged so the client can tell which happened.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
The RFC works through a small hierarchy. The complete local hierarchy is listed with a plain LIST command: an inbox marked as having no inferiors, a Fruit folder with Apple and Banana children, a Tofu folder with no children, and a Vegetable folder with Broccoli and Corn children.

The next example asks for the subscribed mailboxes, using LIST (SUBSCRIBED). The results differ from what LSUB would return. The inbox is subscribed. Fruit/Banana is subscribed. Fruit/Peach is subscribed but does not actually exist, perhaps because it was deleted while still subscribed, and comes back with both the Subscribed and NonExistent attributes. The Fruit folder is not subscribed itself but has two subscribed children. The Vegetable folder is subscribed and has two children, one of which, Vegetable/Broccoli, is subscribed as well.
sections.plainLanguage: In the example, a subscribed folder that has been deleted still shows up, marked as subscribed and as not existing. That is the case where the new command gives more than the old one did.

sections.title: The Formal Syntax
sections.content:
The syntax is given in Augmented Backus-Naur Form, with terms not defined there taken from the IMAP4 specification. The version of the mailbox-list production, which defines the payload of the LIST response, updates the version defined in the IMAP specification, and is pointed to by the mailbox-data production.

The grammar splits the selection options into three groups. Base options can be used on their own. Independent options do not interact syntactically with other options. Modifying options require a base option to also be present, which is how RECURSIVEMATCH is constrained. The return options are given after the RETURN keyword in parentheses.
sections.plainLanguage: The grammar records that RECURSIVEMATCH cannot be used on its own, and that the return options come after a RETURN keyword in brackets.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
This document describes syntactic changes to the specification of the IMAP4 commands LIST, LSUB, RLIST and RLSUB, and the modified LIST command has the same security considerations as those commands.

The Child Mailbox Extension provides a client a more efficient means of determining whether a particular mailbox has children. If a mailbox has children but the currently authenticated user does not have access to any of them, the server should respond with a HasNoChildren attribute. In many cases, however, a server may not be able to efficiently compute whether a user has access to any child mailbox. If such a server responds with a HasChildren attribute when in fact the user has no access to any child mailboxes, potentially more information is conveyed about the mailbox than intended. In most situations this is not a security concern, because if information about whether a mailbox has children is considered sensitive, a user would not be granted access to that mailbox in the first place. The CHILDINFO extended data item has the same security considerations as the HasChildren attribute.
sections.plainLanguage: The new attributes can reveal that a folder has subfolders even when the user cannot open them. The RFC calls this out and asks servers to report no children where they can, on the grounds that a user who cannot open a folder usually should not have been given it at all.

viz.caption: THE MAILBOX ATTRIBUTES THIS EXTENSION ADDS

items.label: Subscribed
items.desc: The mailbox name is subscribed to.

items.label: NonExistent
items.desc: The mailbox name does not refer to an existing mailbox. It implies \NoSelect.

items.label: Remote
items.desc: The mailbox is a remote mailbox.

items.label: HasNoChildren
items.desc: The mailbox has no child mailboxes the authenticated user can access.

cells: May not reflect the actual status of the mailbox
The mailbox is not subscribed itself but has subscribed children
Some servers must do significant extra work

viz.caption: THE SUBSCRIBED EXAMPLE FROM THE RFC

messages.label: LIST (SUBSCRIBED) "" "*"
messages.note: Ask for the names the user is subscribed to.

messages.label: LIST (\Subscribed \NonExistent) "Fruit/Peach"
messages.note: A subscribed name whose mailbox no longer exists.

viz.caption: THE RULES FOR RETURNING A LIST RESPONSE

items.title: One response per name
items.text: The server returns at most one LIST response for each matching mailbox name, so a client never has to merge several responses.

items.title: Two reasons to include a name
items.text: The name itself meets the selection criteria, or one of its descendants does and does not match the pattern itself.

items.title: Attributes are additive
items.text: Attributes in the same response combine, so \Subscribed with \NonExistent means the mailbox is subscribed but does not exist.
